Domestic violence doesn’t always leave bruises—but it can still be deadly. 😔 In No Visible Bruises, Rachel Louise Snyder pulls back the curtain on how abuse is often misunderstood, minimized, or missed entirely—by friends, communities, and even the systems meant to protect people. Through survivor stories and reporting with advocates and law enforcement, she shows how warning signs can hide in plain sight and why leaving isn’t a simple “just walk away” moment. The book also points to real, practical ways prevention and intervention can work—when we stop relying on myths and start taking patterns, risk, and safety seriously. 💜 What’s one myth about domestic violence you’ve heard that you wish people would unlearn—and why? 🗣️  🔗 https://zpr.io/Lh74aZA482mQ #NoVisibleBruises #EndDomesticViolence #DomesticViolenceAwareness #SurvivorVoices #DVBookClub

Join the City of Chattanooga Team Chattanooga , a vibrant and growing community of over 190,000 residents within a metropolitan area of nearly 600,000 is known as the "Scenic City" for a reason. Nestled along the Tennessee River and surrounded by the foothills of the Appalachian Mountains, we are a hub of outdoor adventure and innovation. Home to the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga (UTC) and Chattanooga State Community College , our city blends a rich industrial history with a tech-forward future—famously powered by the nation’s first community-wide "Gig" fiber-optic network.​ The City of Chattanooga was also recently designated as a "National Park City,” the first of its kind in the United States. Our Organization As a City, we are powered by a dedicated workforce of approximately ​ 2,600 employees committed to excellence in public service and making Chattanooga the best community in the country. Our team ensures our city thrives through a wide range of municipal services, including: Public Safety: Chattanooga Police and Fire Departments. Infrastructure Utilities: Public Works, Waste Resources, and specialized Stormwater management. Quality of Life: Award-winning Parks and Outdoors and Community Development systems and the Chattanooga Public Library. Transportation: The Chattanooga Metropolitan Airport (CHA) and citywide transit and pedestrian friendly initiatives. Innovation: Leading-edge smart-city programs with a commitment to cutting edge workforce development policies to ensure all our residents can get ahead. Why Choose Chattanooga? The City of Chattanooga’s workforce is the heartbeat of our community. We don't just offer jobs; we offer careers with purpose: making Chattanooga the best city in America. We are committed to being the premier employer of choice in Southeast Tennessee by providing: Competitive Compensation: Robust pay scales that reflect our commitment to our staff. Work-Life Balance: Generous paid time off and flexible scheduling where possible. Exceptional Wellness: Comprehensive health benefits and wellness programs designed for you and your family that deliver savings to you beyond your paycheck, featuring a centralized health clinic and pharmacy for all City employees. . Growth: A focus on professional development and upward mobility within the organization. ​The Great Outdoors: Your Backyard Playground: Chattanooga isn't just near nature, it's immersed in it. As one of the most biodiverse cities in North America, the "Scenic City" offers an ecological richness that few places on earth can claim. Whether you are an adrenaline junkie or a weekend wanderer, world-class adventure is always less than an hour away. ​Vertical Adventures: Scale legendary sandstone cliffs in what is widely considered the premier rock climbing hub of the Southeast. Water Rapids: From the high-octane whitewater kayaking of the Ocoee River to world-class bass fishing and peaceful paddling on the Tennessee River. Trails for Miles: Explore a massive network of mountain biking and hiking trails that wind through lush ridges, hidden waterfalls, and deep river gorges. In Chattanooga, "work-life balance" means you can finish your shift and be at a trailhead or on the water before the sun sets. Our mission is to work together to build a safe, vibrant, and sustainable city for all Chattanoogans. To do that, it takes a team of skilled and passionate individuals. After years of service protecting the Chattanooga community, the Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) is honoring the retirement of two members of its K9 Unit: K9 Burt, a decorated patrol and narcotics detection dog, and K9 Duke, who ultimately found his true calling outside of police work. K9 Burt, an 11-year-old Belgian Malinois, retired after 10 years of distinguished service with the CPD. As a narcotics detection canine, Burt was responsible for locating more than $3 million in illegal narcotics and currency during his career. Among his most significant contributions were three separate cases in which he located more than 1,000 fentanyl pills. “K9 Burt exemplified the courage and reliability that every handler hopes for in a partner,” said MPO Luke Timmons, Burt’s handler. “What makes me most proud is that no officers were ever injured by suspects during any of Burt’s deployments.” Having a single handler for an entire working career is a rarity among police K9s, making the partnership between Burt and Timmons even stronger.  Burt also earned recognition beyond Chattanooga for his exceptional performance in training and competition. He was named the United States Police Canine Association (USPCA) Regional Top Dog in both narcotics detection and dual-purpose certifications. During the USPCA Detector Dog Challenge, Burt earned first place honors in the room-search portion of the competition before an untimely bathroom break during the vehicle-search event derailed his chances at the overall title - even elite, highly trained police dogs go when they have to go. While K9 Duke’s career followed a different, less illustrious path, he will be remembered as part of the Chattanooga Police Department family. Despite many months of extensive training sessions, Duke consistently demonstrated that police work was not of interest to him. Ultimately, the K9 Unit retired Duke early and found him a loving home. Duke was originally purchased using grant funding, and all grant requirements were satisfied before his early retirement. The Chattanooga Police Department thanks both K9 Burt and K9 Duke for their time with the department and recognizes the commitment of the handlers, families, and community members who support the K9 Unit. The Chattanooga Police Department wishes both K9s a long, healthy retirement.

Did you know our team has cleared over 40 downed trees since the beginning of May? Extreme weather conditions can weaken our trees, often leading to them coming down. When precipitation varies widely from extremely dry to extremely wet, this stresses out the tree. Dry conditions cause the tree to prioritize the usage of water often leading them to drop large branches, while wet conditions can weaken the tree's roots, causing the tree to fall altogether. No matter how healthy you may think your tree is, exposure to extreme weather conditions can damage the tree in a short amount of time. Always monitor your large trees for signs of degrading health. Check for things like soil cracking around the base of the tree, exposed roots, and prolonged “soupy” soil conditions. Call local arborists for professional advice on the health of your trees.  In the meantime, plant new trees! Don’t wait until you have one come down to plant another. Trees take years to grow and provide the shade that we admire them for. Late fall and winter are the best times to plant trees. This dormant period means the tree can invest all of its energy into its roots rather than diverting energy to leaf and fruit production. Check out the Chattanooga Tree Project to volunteer at tree plantings this winter and be on the lookout for free tree giveaways around the city.

SCAM ALERT A Hixson family recently reported a paving scam to CPD. According to the family, a man claiming to work for Ace Asphalt and Paving came to their door and offered to pave their driveway. They asked how much it would cost and the man said he needed to measure the driveway to come up with an estimate. Instead of measuring though, he and his crew paved the driveway and then demanded $58,000 from the family. The couple paid, but fortunately, they didn't lose any money because they quickly reported the incident to us. Remember, if you suspect you're the victim of a scam, alert your bank to freeze your account, file a report with your local law enforcement, and report the scam to the FTC.

Chattanooga Police Department welcomes 21 new officers CHATTANOOGA, Tenn.  – The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) today celebrated the graduation 21 cadets from its 20-week police academy. The members of CPD Class 2026-2 came into the academy with a wide range of life experiences and professional backgrounds, but shared a common goal of serving the Chattanooga community. Among the graduates are four military veterans, a former professional football player, a recruit from the Middle East, two whose siblings already serve with CPD, a former wildland firefighter, a personal trainer, and a welder.  "Every officer brings a unique perspective shaped by their own experiences, and that's one of our department's greatest strengths," said Chief John Chambers. "Building a department with people from different backgrounds and professions helps us better understand and serve the diverse community that calls Chattanooga home." The new officers will now begin 16 weeks of field training, working alongside experienced CPD Field Training Officers as they transition into patrol assignments. The graduation ceremony was held at Abba's House in Hixson. CPD thanks Abba's House for providing the event space to celebrate this milestone for the department's newest officers. Congratulations to CPD Academy Class 2026-2! #CPDnews

The best classroom is often the one you create in everyday life. ❤️ Keep it simple. Make it fun. Let it fit your family’s routine. Those little moments add up to BIG learning! Because families are a child’s first teachers and every moment is a chance to learn. 🌟

The Tennessee Cycling & Bike Tennessee Collaborative had a fantastic turnout in Chattanooga on Friday — bringing together partners from the City of Chattanooga, Chattanooga Parks and Outdoors, Outdoor Chattanooga, bike industry leaders, TN state agencies, Southern Off-Road Bicycle Association chapters, and communities across the state who are working to build cycling infrastructure and momentum at home. The Collaborative's mission: Convene communities, cycling industry businesses and leaders, state partners, and nonprofits to strengthen partnerships and grow cycling opportunities and infrastructure across Tennessee. The day included: -  A behind-the-scenes tour of American Bicycle Group, manufacturers of OBED, Litespeed and Quintana Roo Bicycles. -  Lunch at the new Chattanooga Lookouts Erlanger Park, featuring Chattanooga Mayor Tim Kelly, Parks Administrator David Johnson, and Outdoor Chattanooga Director Gail Loveland. -  Bike Tennessee updates from Silas Stoddart and Rob Regg with Tennessee Vacation. -  A panel discussion about elevating cycling events across the state with SORBA Chattanooga, Bike Tennessee, American Bicycle Group, and Tennessee Gravel. - We ended the day with a group bike ride from the historic Craven’s House on Lookout Mountain back to Erlanger Park. Huge thanks to all of our partners who showed up to celebrate and grow cycling across Tennessee!

Tuesday, July 28, 2026 TSMA RESPONSE TONIGHT ON MASSIVE HOUSE FIRE.  This evening, a seventy year old grandmother rescues five children ranging from 2 infant twins, 7 YO and (2) 9 YO’s from a massive house fire on Walden’s Ridge. At 5:30 pm, a 911 call was made reporting a garage fire located at 515 Gentlemen Ridge in Brow Estates subdivision. Walden’s Ridge Emergency Service (WRES) responded and arrived on the scene reporting heavy smoke and fire in the garage. Firefighters worked quickly to establish water supply. WRES requested a large mutual aid response for additional manpower and apparatus. Signal Mountain Fire Department, Chattanooga Fire Department, Dallas Bay VFD, Lone Oak VFD, Red Bank Fire Department and Mutual Aid Chief 6 Mike Williams, and Chattanooga-Hamilton County Rescue responded to the fire scene.  Firefighters worked quickly to get the garage fire under control. However, fire entered the attic and spread quickly throughout the entire roofline. By 6:10 pm, fire officials reported the 13,000 square foot home was fully involved and firefighters were starting  a defensive attack to contain the fire.  Damages are extensive. No injuries were reported but HCEMS was on the scene checking firefighters for potential heat exhaustion. The cause of the fire will be under investigation by the Hamilton County Sheriffs Office. Family will be staying with neighbors.

Pedestrian Struck - Fatality - 5900 block Highway 58 On July 25, 2026 just before 10:00 p.m., Chattanooga Police responded to a pedestrian struck call in the 5900 block of Highway 58. Upon arrival, officers found a 60-year-old man deceased.  CPD's Traffic/DUI Unit responded to conduct the crash investigation. The preliminary investigation determined Vehicle #1 (Acura) was traveling south in the 5900 block of Highway 58 in the right lane of travel. The pedestrian was walking in the roadway in the same lane of travel when the vehicle struck him. The man was pronounced dead at the scene. This information is preliminary and is subject to change as the investigation continues. Chattanooga Police ask anyone with information regarding this incident to call 423-698-2525. #CPDnews

The preliminary investigation determined both men were in the 1100 block of Arlington Avenue and possessed firearms. The exact details are still under investigation and all leads are being followed.  CPD Homicide and Crime Scene Units responded to investigate and process the scene.  This information is preliminary and subject to change as the investigation continues. Chattanooga Police ask anyone with information regarding this incident to call 423-698-2525. #CPDnews
